chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Dāwūd ibn al-Nuʿmān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about tayammum,

So he said: ʿAmmār was affected by janabah, so he rolled about as an animal rolls. Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to him, while jesting with him: O ʿAmmār, you rolled about as an animal rolls.
So we said to him: How is tayammum? Then he placed his hands upon the ground, then raised them, and wiped his face and his hands a little above the wrists.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, the dry ablution performed with earth when water is unavailable or unusable
key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.تَمَعَّكَ: he rolled himself about on the ground
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring purification
key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: his face, one of the parts wiped in tayammum
key_terms.يَدَيْهِ: his two hands, which are wiped in tayammum

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed according to the hadith of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about ʿAmmār?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of tayammum through the incident of ʿAmmār and the instruction of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It shows that tayammum is performed by striking the earth and wiping the face and hands, rather than imitating full bodily cleansing.
